title: Give every train exactly one route or a typed single-route assessment

facts.note: Subject kind is train; route counting reads every registered interlocking's routes.
Validation runs at CONFIRM over all registered trains regardless of the current diff; phase must be supplied by the harness.

fires: At CONFIRM, a newly registered train is selected by no registered interlocking route and has no route_space declaration.
At CONFIRM, a pre-existing registered train has neither route nor typed assessment, even though the current change touched no train or route.
A train is route-targeted (exactly one route) and also declares route_space.classification single-route.
A train declares single-route with a free-prose basis instead of a closed-vocabulary basis.
An interlocking is unregistered or a route removed/retargeted, leaving a train with neither route nor typed assessment.
A train is selected by routes in two registered interlockings (count 2, so not route-targeted) and declares no typed single-route assessment.
doesNotFire: A train selected by exactly one route across all registered interlockings and declaring no single-route classification.
A train that is not route-targeted and declares route_space.classification single-route with a closed-vocabulary basis.
Phases other than CONFIRM (the check is confirm-blocking; earlier phases are not gated, though the planner should already author compliant trains).

given: The plan's registered trains and the routes of all registered interlockings.
when: The plan reaches CONFIRM (every registered train is checked, whatever changed).
then: Make each registered train exactly one of: route-targeted (selected by exactly one route across all registered interlockings) or typed single-route (route_space.classification single-route with a closed-vocabulary basis) — never both, never neither.
prefer: Route-targeted: exactly one route across all registered interlockings selects the train.
Typed single-route: classification single-route plus a basis from the closed vocabulary.
avoid: No route and no classification, assuming that implies direct dispatch — an omission (issue #1554).
Declaring single-route on a route-targeted train — a contradiction.
Free prose as the single-route basis.
Treating a train selected by zero or several routes as route-targeted; only a count of exactly one qualifies.
why: Route-space was optional metadata, so a train with no route analysis looked like one whose analysis concluded single-route; silence read as proof analysis happened. Explicit classification surfaces the omission at planning time.
evidence: On failure the report carries train_id, train_path, route_ids, classification, basis and admission_status for each offending train.
verifier_detail: Validation family: coverage; template: source_has_required_target; variant: planner_train_route_space_admission; subject_kind: train.
Phase CONFIRM, enforcement confirm-blocking; severity 4. Evaluates all registered trains, not only changed ones.
route_targeted = train selected by exactly one route counted across every registered interlocking; a count of 0 or more than 1 is not route_targeted.
typed_single_route = route_space.classification == single-route AND basis is a member of the closed vocabulary; free-prose basis does not qualify.
exactly_one: route_targeted XOR typed_single_route; both => contradiction, neither => omission.
failure_evidence fields: train_id, train_path, route_ids, classification, basis, admission_status.
audit: schema_version 1.0.0; source kind: constraint; status: active.

sharedNodes.text: Disposition strict: every finding fails the validator; findings are not advisory.

trace.note: Definition only: count other than one is not route_targeted; no unconditional multi-route ban.
